text:
tara: FYI partner onboarding blocked. Their Next.js Edge preview fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED after we published js-sdk v2.1.0.

ben: Did we change package.json exports recently?

tara: Yes, we tightened the conditional exports and removed main/module to be ESM-first. Looks fine for pure ESM consumers but breaks several bundlers and older Node require() flows.

rahul: Repro from partner: `Error: Package subpath './package.json' is not defined by "exports"` when edge runtime tries to read package.json, and `Cannot find module` for require() consumers on node14.

sdk-bot: Patch suggestion: reintroduce main & module fallbacks and explicitly export ./package.json. Minimal snippet: {
  "main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
  "module": "dist/esm/index.js",
  "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
    },
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  }
}
This fixes most esbuild/vite/vercel cases.

ben: Short-term: cut 2.1.1 with that patch and add a smoke test that builds our sample with vercel builder and runs node14 require() check.

ci-bot: Agreed. Add node 14/16/18 matrix and vercel-preview job to CI.

rahul: Long-term: keep main/module indefinitely and add automated tests for conditional export resolution across bundlers and edge runtimes. Also audit sample apps so they don't import internal subpaths like "@redwood/inference/lib" which require explicit subpath exports.

tara: I'll open the PR with package.json changes + tiny sample smoke test. tagging release team and partner.

ben: Also document this in the SDK migration guide: explain that changing exports can break bundlers and edge runtimes, include compatibility snippet.

ci-bot: Release candidate 2.1.1-rc created; CI smoke green.

tara: Thanks team. Follow-ups: PR (tara), CI matrix (ci-bot), samples audit (ben), docs blurb (rahul).
